Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim reference.
Q: Understood. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in the parking lot of a shopping center in Sugar Land, Texas. I'd just pulled into a spot near the main
entrance.
Q: What time of day was it, roughly?
A: Late afternoon, maybe around five. It was still bright out.
Q: Walk me through what happened as you were backing out.
A: I checked my mirrors and didn't see anything behind me, so I started reversing slowly. Then I felt a bump on the
driver's side and heard a scraping sound. The other vehicle was coming down the aisle without slowing much.
Q: Did you stop before you hit anything, or did the other car make contact with you?
A: I stopped right away once I felt the bump. The other car's front corner was against my rear quarter panel.
Q: Were there any witnesses or security cameras you're aware of?
A: A woman near a cart return saw it and said something to me afterward. I don't know if the lot has cameras.
Q: Did you get out and speak with the other driver?
A: Yes, we exchanged information. He seemed rushed but polite.
Q: Are you injured?
A: My lower back is sore. I think I twisted when I turned to look over my shoulder. I had some stiffness that night and
it's still bothering me when I sit for long periods.
Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the next day. They diagnosed a back strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a
referral for physical therapy.
Q: Is there anything you'd like to add or correct in this statement?
A: No, I think that covers it. I'm happy to provide the photos I took at the scene.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>

"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
